record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Determine conditions under which the Petrie scheme of a chiral polytope is acoptic, meaning that each proper face is contained in at most one flag of the Petrie scheme.

evidence.quote: Problem 7 Determine conditions under which the Petrie scheme of a chiral polytope is acoptic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An (abstract) polytope of rank $n$ is a partially ordered set $\mathcal{P}$ with a least face $F_{-1}$ and a greatest face $F_n$, in which every maximal chain (called a flag) has exactly $n+2$ elements, which is strongly flag-connected, and which satisfies the diamond condition: whenever $F < G$ with $\operatorname{rank}(G)-\operatorname{rank}(F)=2$, there are exactly two faces $H$ with $F<H<G$. Two flags are $i$-adjacent ($0\le i\le n-1$) if they differ exactly in their face of rank $i$; the unique flag $i$-adjacent to a flag $\Phi$ is denoted $\Phi^i$.

The polytope $\mathcal{P}$ is called chiral if its automorphism group has exactly two orbits on flags, with adjacent flags lying in different orbits.

The Petrie scheme through a base flag $\Phi_0$ is the sequence of flags
$$\Phi_0,\ \Phi_1,\ \Phi_2,\ \dots$$
defined recursively by
$$\Phi_{k+1} = \Phi_k^{\,i_k}, \qquad \text{where } i_k \equiv k \pmod{n},$$
that is, one applies the adjacencies $0,1,2,\dots,n-1,0,1,\dots$ cyclically until the sequence closes up to $\Phi_0$. The Petrie scheme is called acoptic if every proper face of $\mathcal{P}$ is contained in at most one flag of the scheme (so the scheme does not "self-intersect" through any proper face).

Problem. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on a chiral abstract polytope $\mathcal{P}$ under which its Petrie scheme is acoptic.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not surface a paper resolving the question of when the Petrie scheme of a chiral polytope is acoptic. The notion of acoptic Petrie scheme appears in Williams' 2005 paper on Petrie schemes and is referenced in subsequent work on chiral polyhedra and Petrie–Coxeter constructions, but no source explicitly characterizing acopticity for chiral polytopes was found.

status_evidence.title: Petrie Schemes — Gordon Williams (Canad. J. Math. 2005)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces Petrie schemes for abstract polytopes and the notion of acoptic Petrie schemes; does not settle the chiral case.
status_evidence.claim: Defines acoptic Petrie schemes but does not give the conditions for chiral polytopes.

status_evidence.title: Chiral polytope — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of chiral polytopes; no mention of a resolution to the acoptic Petrie scheme question.
status_evidence.claim: No characterization of acoptic Petrie schemes for chiral polytopes is reported.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry of Polytopes and Polyhedra (Schulte, Handbook chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of symmetry of polytopes including chiral polytopes; the question on acoptic Petrie schemes for chiral polytopes is not reported as resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys do not record a solution.
